questions.q: What is the programme mainly about?
options: What Bitcoin is and how people get it
How banks print new money
The history of coins and notes
How to save money for the future
questions.why: Dan explains the crypto-currency Bitcoin: how it differs from normal money and how new bitcoins are made.

questions.q: What is the first way Bitcoin is different from normal currencies?
options: Its value never changes
It can only be used in one country
It is controlled by the big banks
It isn't issued by governments or banks
questions.why: Dan says it's not printed by governments or banks, so it's not legal tender.

questions.q: Because Bitcoin isn't official money, what can't you do with it?
options: Buy things online
Pay your taxes
Sell it to other people
Watch its value change
questions.why: Neil says that means we can't use it to pay taxes or settle debts, and Dan agrees.

questions.q: What is the second difference between Bitcoin and other money?
options: It is made of a special metal
It is only used by criminals
It exists almost only online
It is worth the same everywhere
questions.why: Dan says it's a digital currency that, apart from a few tokens, largely exists online only.

questions.q: Why can't Neil just say he has a million bitcoins?
options: Because a bank checks every account at the end of each day
Because there are only a million bitcoins in the world in total
Because a system stops cheating: you must trade or 'mine' them
Because the government would arrest him for lying about money
questions.why: Dan says Bitcoin has a process to stop cheating; you either trade for them or go mining.

options: Using your computer to check other Bitcoin payments
Digging underground for special metal tokens
Buying bitcoins from a bank at a lower price
Guessing the future value of Bitcoin each week
questions.why: Neil explains your computer runs calculations to verify other transactions, and you're rewarded with bitcoins.

questions.q: According to Rory Cellan-Jones, what do investors believe?
options: Bitcoin will soon be worth less than $1,000
The big banks will start using Bitcoin
Bitcoin will lose value very quickly
Bitcoin will keep rising, though more slowly
questions.why: He says investors believe it will continue to rise in value, 'albeit at a slower rate'.

questions.q: How does Neil feel about Bitcoin by the end?
options: He wants to start mining bitcoins at home immediately
He thinks it's probably better not to get involved
He plans to invest all his savings in it next week
He is sure it will replace normal money soon
questions.why: After hearing about the banks' doubts, Neil says 'maybe it's best I don't get involved'.
